messages.subject: Error Running on a Linux Cluster
messages.subject_clean: Error Running on a Linux Cluster
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I am currently attempting to run NicheMapR on one of my universities clusters (running CentOS Linux 7). The plan is to run it in a loop using foreach as I will be covering ~93,000 points.  However, I am currently getting a crash every time I attempt to run a simple test of the micro_global model on the cluster (despite it working fine on my local machine).  On my local windows machine, I am able to get it to run for a single point, as well as running it in a loop covering a subset of 100 of my points with no issue (including running the loop in paralell). However, I am getting an immediate error when running even the default micro_global on the cluster.  It seems like it might be related to this issue (https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/issues/3?_pjax=%23js-repo-pjax-container).  However, I am new to Linux, Cluster Computing, and relatively new to NicheMapR so it might be something completely different, and maybe a cluster issue rather than a NicheMapR issue, I am not sure.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

I'm not completely organised yet on the Linux front, so there could be something awry. You're getting a segfault and it looks like you're using your own interface script to the Fortran programs. It's possible you're not sending in the right number of items and the model is pushing through on a Windows machine but the issue is being caught on Linux. That can happen. I'd suggest for starters that you see if you can get the micro_global function to run on your system. If you get the same problem, then we know it's something more fundamental about the Linux compile. If micro_global runs, then the problem might lie in your script.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Offline global climate install
messages.body_plain:
G'day NicheMapRs,

I'm trying to set up NicheMapR again on a computer that doesn't connect to the web. It's been inefficient, but not impossible. Where I'm stuck is that line "get.global.climate()". Clearly, not internet, no download. Does anybody know of a way to get it to download off a stick or an external drive? As far as I can tell, I should even have the data on the computer in question, if the data is the micro_clim.ncdf data set. I just don't know how to make NicheMapR recognise that I already have it.

Hints and tips welcome.

Cheers

Sean

messages.subject: Re: Offline global climate install
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sean,

Easy, just make your own micro_global script and comment out the lines:

    # load global climate files
    gcfolder<-paste(.libPaths()[1],"/gcfolder.rda",sep="")
    if(file.exists(gcfolder)==FALSE){
      message("You don't appear to have the global climate data set - \n run function get.global.climate(folder = 'folder you want to put it in') .....\n exiting function micro_global")
      opt <- options(show.error.messages=FALSE)
      on.exit(options(opt))
      stop()
    }
    load(gcfolder)

and replace them with

folder <- "name of your folder"

Then the following code later on will work:

global_climate<-raster::brick(paste(folder,"/global_climate.nc <http://global_climate.nc>",sep=""))
soilmoisture<-suppressWarnings(raster::brick(paste(folder,"/soilw.mon.ltm.v2.nc <http://soilw.mon.ltm.v2.nc>",sep="")))

Note though that it isn't 'micro_clim.ncdf' that's being used, but rather the two files noted in the code just above.

All the best,
Mike
